name: Aperture Cinema
description: A single-file H5 cinema booking app. The distinctive surface is a 2D seat map: choosing seats is spatial selection on a 6x10 grid with aisles, taken seats, accessible spaces and premium rows, not a pick from a list. On top of it sits a cross-field constraint — the ticket-type counts must add up to exactly the number of seats chosen or checkout stays shut. 12 screens, 6 films with generated posters, 11 showings, member points, cancellations that put seats back on sale.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — the seat map serialises row by row into free / SELECTED / taken lists with the exact test-id pattern, so a text-only agent can pick seats as precisely as a viewer.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view. For the verifier only.

world.money: every price is held in pence, so all totals are exact integer arithmetic
world.seats: rows A-F, ten per row, aisles after seat 2 and seat 8; rows D and E cost £2.00 more per seat; F1 and F2 are accessible spaces
world.occupancy: which seats are taken lives in state, so booking and cancelling change availability for the rest of the episode and reset cleanly
world.points: 100 points is £1.00 off; spending them deducts from the member balance and a cancellation refunds them
